definition: Digital applications for climate adaptation provide users with information, recommendations or decision support specifically intended to help them respond or adapt to climate risks. Counts when the project finances, develops, procures or deploys an application or digital service with an explicit adaptation function, such as climate-informed agricultural advice, drought-management support or adaptation decision tools. The application must support an adaptation decision or action; merely displaying climate information belongs to climate_information_systems. Does not count for climate-smart practices with no digital component, generic digital services with no stated adaptation function, climate information provided only as context, or applications developed outside the project. The application must turn climate or weather information into a specific decision or action: advice to users (when to plant, how much to irrigate, which variety to choose, how to protect stock or property), prioritising investments or maintenance, or selecting who receives support; a data platform, dashboard or portal that only makes climate information available is climate_information_systems. A system that also issues alerts may count under ews as well. Does not count: supply-chain or logistics systems; preparedness simulations or drills; programmes that incubate startups which may build such tools.
boundary: The project uses climate information digitally to decide or act against climate risk: advice to users, prioritising investments or maintenance, or selecting who receives support.
note: Keep distinct from climate_information_systems and ews.
